newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Hong Kong banks borrow.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Hong Kong banks borrow.

text.p: Asian debt markets spent another quiet day on Friday.
Dao Heng Bank increased its three-year floating rate certificate of deposit issue to HK$1.5 billion from HK$1.2 billion, arranger HSBC Markets said. The sell-down rate was 49 percent, it said.
The certificates were issued at par to float at 36 basis points over the three-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate. With fees, the all-in return for top-tier managers is 43.5 basis points.
There had been rumours that the Dao Heng deal wasn't progressing very well because there had been a lot of Hong Kong dollar FRCDs brought to the market all at once.
But, in the end, the Dao Heng deal was increased just as most of the other LAF-eligible bank FRCDs launched this year have been.
LAF, or the Liquidity Adjustment Facility, is the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's discount windonw.
Eligibility for LAF tends to make an issue more attractive to banks because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase agreements with the monetary authority, increasing liquidity.
Bank of East Asia today signed its HK$2.3 billion FRCD, which had been increased from HK$1.8 billion.
Bankers said they don't expect to see any major Hong Kong dollar-denominated issues for the rest of 1996.
"It looks like it is pretty much finished for this year," said one syndicate manager.
Another Hong Kong bank, Liu Chong Hing Bank, launched a US$80 million issue via Citicorp International.
The five-year FRCD's have a put option in year three. They were issued at par to float at 40 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return is 50.42 basis points.
Chase Manhattan Asia released terms on its upcoming US$100 million floating rate note issue for Korea First Bank .
The three-year FRN has a coupon of 35 basis points over LIBOR. It will be priced at par and re-offered at 99.865 to give a yield of 40 basis points on a discounted basis.
With fees, the all-in to top-tier managers that take the paper at par is 43.5 basis points.
In other news, Standard and Poor's Corp has assigned a BB-minus rating to AES China Generating Co Ltd's US$180 million senior unsecured notes due in 2006.
AES China Generating is expected to launch a Yankee bond. Morgan Stanley is tipped as the lead.
